title: Level 3 (Advanced) - B-17
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 4♠. South should take care to ruff the opening diamond lead with a trump other than the ♠2. The North-South spade combination is certainly strong enough to withstand this play.

By preserving the ♠2, South will be in a position to eventually cross to the North hand by leading the ♠2 to the ♠3. As South's plan should involve developing a diamond trick for North, dummy entries will be important.

South has 2 certain heart losers, and 1 certain club loser. As West is likely to have the ♣K, 2 club losers are a serious possibility. South can succeed by trading 2 of these 4 losers for 2 diamond losers. In the process, a winner will be established taking care of 1 of South's other 2 losers.

South should cross to the dummy in trump (again preserving the ♠2) and lead a diamond from North. When East plays low, South discards a heart (discarding a club is just as good). West will win and switch to a heart, South winning the ♥A.

As the trumps are 2-1, the contract is certain. South again crosses to dummy in trumps (still preserving the ♠2) and repeats the diamond play. North now has a diamond winner to take care of 1 of South's club losers. The ♠2 can be played to the ♠3 to reach the dummy.

South could have done equally well by not ruffing at trick 1. Instead, he immediately discards a heart. The play will continue similarly. As before, South must be careful not to use the ♠2 early. If East has a diamond honour, it would not help him to cover North's diamond plays at any point. South can simply ruff (not with the ♠2) and continue to set up a diamond trick in North's hand.
